name: Mali
snapshot: An al-Qaeda affiliate's fuel blockade cut Bamako's power to a few hours a day, while the junta dissolved political parties and tied itself ever closer to Russia.
culture: Mali was the heart of medieval empires whose wealth in gold made Mansa Musa legendary, and Timbuktu's manuscripts and mud mosques testify to centuries of Islamic scholarship. Its music is famous worldwide, from the desert blues of Ali Farka Touré and Tinariwen to the kora of Toumani Diabaté. Bambara is the most widely spoken language.
society: Gold is the main export, and the junta has pushed foreign miners for a bigger share. Jihadist groups and Tuareg separatists have fought the state since 2012. The army and Russian mercenaries have been accused of massacres, notably at Moura in 2022. Hundreds of schools are closed, and millions need food aid.
situation: Mali's soldiers seized power in 2020 and again in 2021, promising to do what the French army and UN peacekeepers had not: defeat the jihadists. They expelled the French, brought in Russian Wagner mercenaries and formed an alliance with fellow juntas in Burkina Faso and Niger. In 2026, the jihadists brought the war to the capital's doorstep.

The al-Qaeda-linked JNIM began blockading fuel tankers from Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire in September 2025, cutting Bamako's electricity to six hours a day and closing schools. The blockade eased early this year. Then on 25 April, JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front launched coordinated offensives, and Defence Minister Sadio Camara, architect of the Russia partnership, was killed. On 28 April JNIM declared all roads into Bamako closed (Africanews). Junta leader Assimi Goïta disappeared from view for days before reappearing on television to insist the situation was "under control." By July, JNIM had pushed into southern Mali for the first time and was imposing hijab rules on public transport outside the capital. "If Mali collapses, everything collapses," a senior diplomat warned (Reuters via Gazette). Analysts think JNIM lacks the strength to take Bamako but could strangle the junta into negotiating, or into a coup from within.
power: A military junta. Goïta made himself president for a renewable five-year term in 2025 without an election, dissolved political parties and rules by decree with a transitional council. Mali left ECOWAS and formed the Alliance of Sahel States with Burkina Faso and Niger.

story: The empires of Ghana, Mali and Songhai made this the heart of medieval West Africa; Mansa Musa's 14th-century pilgrimage to Mecca was so lavish it crashed the price of gold in Cairo, and Timbuktu was a centre of learning. France conquered it in the 1890s. After independence in 1960 came dictatorship, then democracy in 1992. A Tuareg rebellion in 2012 let jihadists seize the north; France intervened, then was expelled by the juntas that took power in 2020 and 2021.
